As one who has worked in the field I can tell you a little bit about how recalls work. There are only 19 states, plus WA, DC that allow recall petitions, each having different laws covering them. If a state allows say 40% of registered voters on a petition to initiate a recall election, it is then submitted to the Registrar of Voters for verification of signors, all within a specified time frame. Time frames will vary by state. At that point custodian of petition is relinquished and Registrar submits it to the Secretary of State, who will then issue a Proclamation.

Problem lies with number of petitions circulating. If Change.org has one, Avaaz.org another, along with a few more, Registrar will not know how many petitions are going around, nor the time frame they are due. They do not wait for all possible petitions to come in, then consolidate them into one. They are under a time limit on each submitted.

It's tricky, and frustrating I know. But the reality is the law stands, and no amount of name calling will change that.
